title: Compact Burst Slimming: kernel-aware microbatch orchestrator to minimize padding and decode stalls
creator: Maya Patel
description: Problem: In bursty workloads we observe inefficient packing of short and medium-length requests into GPU batches which produces excessive padding tokens, suboptimal kernel choices, and transient decode stalls when prefill and decode phases collide. This ticket implements a compact burst slimming orchestrator: a microbatch-level controller that shapes incoming burst traffic into compact microbatches using run-length heuristics, kernel hinting, and prefill/decode phase separation to reduce pad overhead and avoid stall cascades.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end integration into runtime request pipeline with opt-in feature flag
Measured pad token reduction >= 28% on synthetic burst benchmark compared to baseline packing
No more than 5% regression in median latency for tail-sensitive SLAs; P99 latency improvement for burst scenarios
Kernel hints emitted for at least 95% of shaped microbatches and result in expected kernel selection in runtime heuristics
Automated unit and integration tests covering run-length heuristics, prefill/decode separation, and kernel hint propagation
technical_notes: Design uses a short-term sliding window (burst horizon) to detect burst starts and derive a compact packing target for the next N ms
Run-length heuristics: collapse identical trailing padding footprints across requests within the burst window to enable pad elision during prefill
Kernel hinting: annotate microbatch metadata with expected effective sequence length, sparsity flag, and preferred kernel family to guide compile-time kernel selection
Prefill/decode separation: schedule prefill work earlier and gate decoder token emission to avoid simultaneous kernel contention on shared GPU resources
Fallbacks: if shaped microbatch cannot meet latency SLO, revert to latency-first packing; explicit telemetry emitted for every fallback
Interaction with KV cache: shaped prefill must preserve KV cache slot mapping for subsequent decode calls — mapping maintained by microbatch ID translation layer
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (spike): prototype burst horizon detector and run-length elision in a non-blocking simulator (2w)
Phase 2: implement microbatch shaping controller in runtime ingress path, add kernel hint metadata, add feature flag (3w)
Phase 3: integrate with scheduler to separate prefill and decode windows, add gating logic and telemetry hooks (2w)
Phase 4: internal canary, metrics dashboard, and iterate on heuristics (2w)
Phase 5: rollout to larger fleet and add automated regression alerts tied to prompt set evals (1w)
qa_plan: Unit tests for run-length elision logic and microbatch ID translation
Integration tests that run end-to-end prefill->decode flows with KV cache validation
Synthetic burst benchmarks across representative length distributions (short, mixed, long)
Load test to validate no CPU/GPU oversubscription and to measure P50/P95/P99 latency changes
Chaos test: simulate node GPU slowdown and ensure graceful fallback to latency-first packing
rollouts_and_metrics: Feature gated rollout: start with 5% of small-hosted pool, expand to 20% after 48h, freeze if pad reduction < 20% or P99 regresses > 10%
Key metrics: pad_tokens_per_request, tokens_served_per_gpu_sec, prefill_decode_overlap_ratio, kernel_switch_rate, p50/p95/p99 latency
Target improvements: pad_tokens_per_request -30% (target), prefill_decode_overlap_ratio < 0.1, kernel_switch_rate reduced by 15%
Dashboards: create per-model and per-region panels for shaped vs baseline comparison, include waterfall of prefill vs decode durations
